sentences.text: Aurornis possessed clawed wings and a long bony tail.
Fossil evidence shows traces of downy feathers on Aurornis's tail, chest, and neck.
The species Aurornis xui was first described and named in 2013 by a team led by Pascal Godefroit.
The species name A. xui honors the paleontologist Xu Xing.
The absence of large feathers suggests that Aurornis xui was incapable of flight.
A 2013 phylogenetic analysis placed Aurornis within the avian lineage, in a position more basal than Archaeopteryx.
A 2017 re-evaluation of the Harlem Archaeopteryx specimen found Aurornis to be an anchiornithid.
Aurornis is classified within the unranked family Avialae.
Aurornis belongs to the family Anchiornithidae.
Analysis confirmed Aurornis came from the Tiaojishan Formation, dated to the late Jurassic (Oxfordian stage) approximately 160 million years ago.
Fossil remains of Aurornis have been found in the Tiaojishan Formation of Liaoning, China.
A 2014 analysis by Brusatte et al. recovered Aurornis outside Avialae, classifying it as a troodontid closely related to Anchiornis.
The classification of A. xui as a bird is controversial because there are multiple different definitions of the word "bird".
Paleontologist Luis Chiappe argued that the forelimb of A. xui is too short to be that of a true bird.
A 2017 study suggested that Aurornis might be a junior synonym of Anchiornis because its traits fall within Anchiornis's range of variation.
